curriculum.lesson_evidence: Choose nouns, verbs and adjectives to make sentences precise and readable.
curriculum.scope_limit: Individual Written Core lesson contributes partial evidence; independently verify syllabus content-point alignment.

lesson.child_mission: Choose nouns, verbs and adjectives to make sentences precise and readable.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Keep the independent response and two written check responses; record oral retelling or performance where required by the task.
lesson.extension: Create a new example using a completely different character or setting, show the same skill, then explain to another person how you checked its accuracy.
lesson.guided_practice:
WE DO — attempt each prompt before comparing to the feedback.
1. Find two nouns in "A pelican balanced on the post".
COMPARE: Pelican and post are nouns. Balanced is an action verb.
2. Swap "went" for a more specific verb in "The cyclist went downhill".
COMPARE: "The cyclist coasted downhill" explains the manner of movement more precisely.
3. Add one helpful adjective to "The lantern hung above the door".
COMPARE: "The cracked lantern hung above the door" gives condition. Many other precise choices are possible.
4. Improve "The car moved on the road" with one precise noun, verb and adjective.
COMPARE: Example: "The rusty ute rattled along the gravel road." Ute and road are nouns; rattled is verb; rusty and gravel specify details.
lesson.independent_task:
YOU DO — complete the following substantial original task, not a copied model.
Analyse the nouns, main verb and adjectives in "The determined ranger carried a heavy bag along the dusty track." Then revise three sentences of your own about a beach, a library and a storm. Label one noun, verb and adjective in each revised sentence and explain the improvement.
lesson.learning_intention: Choose nouns, verbs and adjectives to make sentences precise and readable.
lesson.offline_alternative: Use paper to copy only the original independent prompt; have the child respond in writing or orally as required. Save a photograph or brief parent observation for the learning record.
lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance: Require accurate word classifications; determined, heavy and dusty modify nouns; carried is action. Different correct descriptive revisions accepted. Accept plausible original solutions where the text supports them; require the learner to explain at least one independent choice.

Parent: Written model 1: Original demonstration: "The mechanic repaired a bicycle." Mechanic and bicycle name things; repaired tells the action.

Parent: Written model 2: Common error: Adding four similar adjectives can weaken rather than strengthen a sentence. Correction: "The cracked lantern hung above the door" gives condition. Many other precise choices are possible.

Parent: Assess comprehension and language rather than penalising speech or motor difficulties unrelated to the objective. Keep written models out of the child role.
